enum: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies
JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Not applicable / No information: the article is a non-systematic narrative synthesis and secondary descriptive overview rather than a primary longitudinal cohort or trial; for the two-season Mamirauá study summarized second-hand (June flood and November dry season 2008, PDF pp. 9-10), participant or household attrition between campaigns is not reported.
cross_tool_domains.confounding: High concern (uncontrolled): state-level comparisons between GDP per capita growth and household water/sewage network coverage (2002-2009, PDF pp. 3-5) are purely descriptive and bivariate, with no multivariable adjustment for rurality, population density, municipal fiscal capacity, or hydrological dispersion; local case vignettes likewise report unadjusted descriptive proportions.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Weak (contextual mention only): 'Amazônia Legal' denotes the 9-state Brazilian geopolitical macroregion (PDF p. 1) rather than a legal exposure, and institutional or regulatory features—indigenous land status (PDF pp. 6-7), un-metered flat-rate municipal water tariffs of R$ 9.00/month in São Gabriel da Cachoeira (PDF p. 7), sustainable-use reserve status in Mamirauá (PDF p. 9), private concessionaire operation by Águas do Amazonas in Manaus (PDF p. 11), and Ministry of Health drinking-water standard Portaria 518/2004 in Novo Israel (PDF p. 12)—are cited only descriptively without systematic legal coding.
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Moderate to high concern: macro-indicators rely on official IBGE secondary sources (2010 Census, 2002-2009 PNAD network connection rates, 2008 MUNIC municipal manager perceptions, and 2002-2009 GDP per capita; PDF pp. 2-5), which measure formal network connection rather than potability or service continuity, while primary water-quality, parasitological, and household interview protocols for the four Amazonas case vignettes are not detailed in this article (summarized from prior publications, PDF pp. 6-12).
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Mixed / secondary descriptive only: state-level water and sanitation outcomes use standardized IBGE PNAD definitions (% permanent private households connected to water supply and sewage networks, PDF p. 3), whereas local case summaries report fecal contamination rates, water-source preferences, self-reported symptoms, and intestinal parasite prevalence second-hand without full denominators, laboratory validation details, or uncertainty intervals in the present text (PDF pp. 6-12).
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: High concern: no review protocol, search strategy, or inclusion criteria exist; case-study statistics are selectively summarized from prior work without confidence intervals or complete sample denominators (e.g., total stool samples for the 57.9%-90.3% parasite prevalence in Mamirauá on PDF p. 10, where in-text citation 'GIATTI et al., 2009' is also omitted from the bibliography), and Table 1 / Graph 1 / Figure 1 appear only as unextracted graphic elements in the PDF text layer.
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: High concern: no systematic literature search or case-selection protocol is used; while the macro-indicator overview covers all 9 states of the Brazilian Legal Amazon using IBGE tabulations (PDF pp. 2-5), the four local case studies (Iauaretê, São Gabriel da Cachoeira, Mamirauá Reserve, and Manaus peripheral neighborhoods Santa Etelvina and Novo Israel; PDF pp. 6-12) are purposively drawn from the authors' own prior research in Amazonas State rather than systematically sampled across the region.

raw_response.overall_narrative_summary: Giatti & Cutolo (2012) is a non-systematic interdisciplinary synthesis essay—lacking a Methods section, primary empirical data collection, statistical hypothesis testing, or systematic review search protocol—that pairs a descriptive overview of secondary IBGE macro-indicators (2002-2009 state GDP per capita and PNAD household water/sewage network coverage across the 9 states of Brazil's Legal Amazon; PDF pp. 2-5) with narrative summaries of previously published local studies in Amazonas State covering Iauaretê (Giatti et al., 2007; Toledo et al., 2009), São Gabriel da Cachoeira (Giatti, 2007), Mamirauá Sustainable Development Reserve (Giatti & Cutolo, 2012), and peripheral neighborhoods of Manaus (Visser et al., 2011; Giatti et al., 2010; Rocha & Horbe, 2006) (PDF pp. 6-12). Because the article neither reports a primary empirical study (quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods, or doctrinal/jurimetric) nor conducts a systematic/scoping review (ruling out AMSTAR 2), chosen_tool is set to NONE. Across cross-tool bias domains, causal and inferential validity is severely limited by purposive selection of the authors' own Amazonas case studies, purely descriptive bivariate state-level comparisons with no confounder control, incomplete second-hand reporting of primary measurement protocols and sample denominators, and purely contextual references to tariff, concession, conservation-unit, and drinking-water quality rules (Portaria MS 518/2004). Note that while all 17 pages of article prose are fully legible, the embedded graphic contents of Figura 1 (p. 2), Tabela 1 (p. 3), and Gráfico 1 (p. 5) are not rendered in the PDF text stream.
raw_response.overall_rating: NOT APPLICABLE (design fits no listed tool)
raw_response.study_design_identified: Non-systematic narrative synthesis / interdisciplinary essay combining descriptive secondary macro-indicators (IBGE Census/PNAD 2002-2010) with narrative summaries of previously published local case studies in Amazonas
raw_response.where_found_summary: Study objectives and overall structure in Introdução (PDF pp. 1-2) and Resumo/Abstract (PDF p. 17); secondary IBGE Census, PIB per capita, PNAD (2002-2009), and MUNIC (2008) descriptive overview in Macroindicadores (PDF pp. 2-5; note Tabela 1 on p. 3 and Gráfico 1 on p. 5 have captions/notes in text while graphic cells are unextracted); second-hand summaries of previously published Amazonas case studies in Estudos de casos — Distrito de Iauaretê (PDF pp. 6-7), São Gabriel da Cachoeira (PDF pp. 7-9), Comunidades ribeirinhas da reserva de desenvolvimento sustentável Mamirauá (PDF pp. 9-10), and Manaus (PDF pp. 10-12); interpretive synthesis in Considerações finais (PDF pp. 13-14) and Referências Bibliográficas (PDF pp. 14-17).
raw_response.why_tool_chosen: Per RISK_OF_BIAS.md §§1-2, NONE is selected because S128 is a non-systematic narrative review/essay with no primary empirical methodology and no systematic literature search. AMSTAR 2 is strictly excluded because there is no search strategy, database query, or screening protocol. Primary quantitative (JBI), qualitative (CASP), and mixed-methods (MMAT) checklists do not apply because the local Amazonas empirical findings (Iauaretê, São Gabriel da Cachoeira, Mamirauá, and Manaus neighborhoods Santa Etelvina and Novo Israel) are narrative summaries of the authors' previously published studies (Giatti, 2007; Giatti et al., 2007, 2010; Visser et al., 2011; Giatti & Cutolo, 2012) paired with descriptive IBGE secondary tabulations. Finally, the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework does not apply because 'Amazônia Legal' refers to the 9-state Brazilian geographic macroregion rather than a legal intervention, and tariff, concessionaire, land-tenure, and Portaria MS 518/2004 references appear only as brief descriptive background rather than a doctrinal, jurimetric, or institutional case-study design.
